concept: CommandPalette is a small appliance sheet with one recessed window to type in and a printed legend of every command underneath. The lit command carries an ink index mark and its keycap shows the shortcut, so nobody opens a menu to learn what the device can do.

default_to_avoid.pattern: command palette: a dark floating box centred high on the page with a blurred backdrop, a glowing selected row and fuzzy-match highlights (cmdk, Raycast, VS Code)
default_to_avoid.why_not: A glowing row and a blurred backdrop spend colour and glass on a body, and a floating dark box has no place in a warm-white appliance where only the display emits light.

default_to_avoid.pattern: command palette that lists commands as full-width coloured rows with a filled accent selection
default_to_avoid.why_not: A filled accent row spends the unit's one orange on a list item, while the legend marks the chosen word with ink and weight.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): every band and station printed on the case, the one in use marked by the pointer
system/FORM.md surface class: Dialog overlay language, elevation.float over a scrim, radius corner.panel
WAI-ARIA APG combobox with a listbox popup, focus stays in the field and aria-activedescendant names the reached row

derivation.consequence: the legend sits beside or around the control that walks it, in one fixed column or arc
derivation.form: The commands stand in one column right under the query window, and the section names are printed on the same inset line, so nothing reflows when the lit command moves.

derivation.consequence: the chosen word carries one ink index mark beside it
derivation.form: The reached command shows one small ink dot at its inline start; the waiting commands keep the same space empty so the words do not shift.

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The query field is a window cut into the sheet with surface.sunken and elevation.well, as in Input, so it reads as a reading and the commands stay flat printing.

derivation.consequence: a legend is flat printing on the material, never a raised part
derivation.form: Commands have no shadow and no raised edge; only the lit one gets a hairline plate, and the shortcuts are Kbd caps.

derivation.consequence: every word is also a target that picks itself, and the control's keys walk it word by word
derivation.form: Each command is a 44px row that runs on a click or Enter, while the arrow keys walk the rows from inside the field, with Home and End for the ends.

derivation.consequence: fast in, slow out, through the state motion tokens
derivation.form: The sheet and scrim arrive over motion.enter and leave over the longer motion.exit, kept mounted by presence until the exit is done.

options.name: query window above a printed legend, ink index mark and plate on the lit row
section names in a fixed left column, a rule beside the lit row
field and list inside one recessed well

variants.reason: A recesses only the window and prints the rest flat, which is P2 and P7 together; B spends a third of the width on section names and breaks down on a phone, and C recesses the list as well, so the legend reads as a part cut into the body instead of printing.

root.why: The sheet is a body of matte plastic with the capped panel radius and the same float elevation as Dialog, over a scrim.

inline.why: A palette shown in place sits in the flow of the page at a fixed place and covers nothing.

well.why: The query window is recessed into the sheet with the inverse light, 44px tall so the whole well is the press area of the field.

mark.why: The printed search mark sits on the inset line at the start of the well and is hidden from assistive tech because the label names the field.

field.why: The query is typed in the body size and primary ink, with the placeholder in secondary ink that still holds 4.5:1.

list.why: The legend is one scrolling column under the window, with a fixed maximum height so the sheet does not reflow as the query narrows it.

group.why: A section keeps its name and its commands together in one block, so the name is printed above the words it covers.

heading.why: A section name is a small label in secondary ink, regular weight, printed on the inset line above its commands.

option.why: Each command is a row of at least 44px, so the whole word is a target a finger can hit.

index.why: The ink dot is the one index mark beside the lit command; it is drawn with a border and a fill so it also shows in forced colours.

text.why: The command name wraps by character so a long name or Thai text never pushes the keycaps out of the row.

keys.why: The shortcut is printed as Kbd caps at the end of the row, so the quick way to run the command is learned from the list.

empty.why: When no command matches, one line in secondary ink says so, and the same words are announced politely.

data-state=open.why: The open sheet and its scrim arrive quickly on the enter easing, all parts at the same moment.

data-state=closing.why: The sheet and scrim leave over the slower exit duration while presence keeps them mounted.

focus-within.why: The query window shows the focus ring while the field has focus, and the ring stays there as the arrows move the lit row.

data-active=true.why: The reached command goes to primary ink and medium weight with a hairline plate and the index mark, with no orange.

aria-disabled=true.why: A command that cannot run stays printed at reduced opacity, is skipped by the arrow keys and ignores Enter and clicks.

data-empty=true.why: With no match the list collapses to the empty line and the field drops its list reference, so nothing stale is read.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduced motion the sheet appears and leaves at once, with no rise and no fade.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the sheet, window and lit row keep real borders and the index mark draws in the highlight colour.

opacity.why: The sheet and scrim fade in fast and out slower, and the index mark appears with the lit row.

transform.why: A short rise of a few pixels is the only travel, with no scale, no bounce and no stagger.

background-color.why: The lit row's plate inks in on the hover duration, because a real key does not rise as the hand nears it.

border-color.why: The plate's hairline changes on the hover duration with its fill, so the pair moves as one.

color.why: A row's ink steps from secondary to primary on the hover duration when it is reached.
